transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-16
Time: 15:00 - 15:55 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood CSM); Elena Martinez (Head of ML, SierraLogic), Marcus Park (CTO), Sophie Lane (Product Lead), Tom Bradley (Infra Eng)

Summary:
Quick QBR covering usage trends (spikes & normalization), cost drivers (token mix, long-context calls), reliability incidents in last quarter, roadmap alignment for deprecation of older model variants, and next-steps to scope a pilot on dedicated capacity. Customer expressed concern about deprecation of the 8k model family used in staging and wants guarantees for feature parity + fallback paths.

Topics covered:
- Usage patterns & growth (conversational bot + long-form summarization)
- Token-level cost breakdown and anomalous bursts
- Latency SLOs and p99 tail incidents (weekend spike)
- Model deprecation risk and compatibility matrix
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
- Security/compliance ask: SOC2 evidence, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Next steps & action owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Reyes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see we have the same agenda as the invite, we'll run through usage, cost, reliability, then priya will do the tech readout. um, quick check — any new folks?
[00:08] Elena Martinez: Hi it's Elena, quick note, still the same team, thanks for holding this QBR.
[00:12] Marcus Park: Marcus here, we'll have Tom answer infra-y questions.
[00:15] Jordan Reyes: Great. Liam quick callout?
[00:17] Liam Chen: Just want to highlight the normalization chart I sent; you had a sustained spike in mid-November that shaved off costs after caching, we can go through that.

[00:30] Priya Kapoor: Ok jumping in — on usage, SierraLogic is at roughly 1.8B tokens/month now, month-on-month +22%. The mix is ~70% short-turn chat calls and ~30% long-context summarization (2k-4k token calls). Those long calls are the dominant cost driver because of the way prefix caching and KV usage behaves.
[00:50] Sophie Lane: Yep that's right, the product team pushed the new transcript summarizer in Oct and it's been super useful, but costs popped up. We thought caching would flatten it but the retokenization for some flows still trips the prefix cache.
[01:06] Priya Kapoor: Right, there's two levers: better prompt engineering and batching settings, and then quantization/model family changes. We flagged a possible 8k->16k migration risk — some of your internal pipelines depend on the older 8k checkpoint that's scheduled for deprecation in Jan.
[01:24] Elena Martinez: This is the big one — we can't lose the behaviour of the 8k family; there's custom normalization the team built. If you deprecate, what guarantees do we get? Also, can we pin a model and still get security patches?
[01:40] Jordan Reyes: Short answer: yes, you can pin a version on Dedicated or Private, and we'll keep security/patch backports for pinned rollouts under a support add-on. We need to scope SLAs. But we also want to propose a migration plan — a canary test and a shadow traffic run to validate outputs.

[02:05] Tom Bradley: From infra side, our primary asks are VPC peering options (we're on AWS eu-west-1), long-term audit logs storage, and KMS integration. We also need to understand egress cost patterns — during the November spike our network showed bursts.
[02:22] Priya Kapoor: For VPC, we support private deployment (customer-managed control plane) and dedicated pools in region; we have docs for VPC peering steps and firewall rules. I'll send the network checklist. On KMS we support external KMS/HSM — we'll include the integration guide.
[02:38] Marcus Park: Can you confirm retention for audit logs and if logs can be routed to our S3? The compliance team needs 12 months, immutable.
[02:46] Jordan Reyes: Yes, audit logs can be exported; retention policies can be configured. We'll share the SOC2 pack and the audit export flow.

[03:10] Priya Kapoor: Switching to reliability — there were two higher-p99 latency incidents last month (Nov 12 and Nov 19) correlated with the heavy summarization batch. Both were due to resource contention on one of the shared GPU queues. We suggested short-term mitigation: autoscale thresholds + temporary burst capacity to Dedicated. For long-term, we recommended isolating long-context routes into a dedicated pool with KV-cache tuning.
[03:38] Elena Martinez: Did you see output regressions when you suggested the quantized variant? We ran a small eval and the summarizer lost named-entity fidelity.
[03:46] Priya Kapoor: That's expected—some quantization/FP16 paths can slightly alter output distribution. Our Optimize team can run targeted evals and tune thresholds (we have a model/quantization recommendation table).
[03:56] Sophie Lane: How soon can we get that evaluation? We need to know if the quantized path is acceptable before the 8k deprecation window.
[04:05] Priya Kapoor: We can do a 2-week eval with a fixed prompt set; that includes divergence metrics and some example outputs. I'll need your canonical prompt set and a small holdout set.

[04:30] Jordan Reyes: On cost — we looked at per-token cost and the November spike added ~18% to the monthly bill due to repeated long-context calls and low cache hit rate. We propose three immediate steps: 1) reduce redundant re-tokenization by rewriting prompts (we can help with best-practices), 2) pin heavy routes to dedicated pool which is cheaper per-token at scale, 3) enable prefix caching + longer TTLs on your summarizer pipeline.
[04:58] Marcus Park: Tying dollars to engineering change is fine but procurement needs committed numbers. What does dedicated reserved capacity pricing look like for your 6-month pilot?
[05:08] Jordan Reyes: I'll share tiered pricing — committed capacity monthly vs pay-as-you-go. For a pilot at your current profile, the committed plan conservatively shows 12–18% savings over hosted at your 1.8B tokens/month profile, depending on model family. I'll get you the spreadsheet.

[05:35] Tom Bradley: Also we need to evaluate data residency if we go private on-prem later. Any blockers?
[05:40] Priya Kapoor: On-prem is supported but it's a heavier lift; we provide an optional on-prem package and a playbook. For now, VPC/private control plane in eu-west-1 would meet residency requirements and is less intrusive.

[06:05] Sophie Lane: Back to deprecation: we need a staged timeline. It can't be a hard cutoff. We need a compatibility matrix to map 8k behaviors to the new checkpoints.
[06:15] Priya Kapoor: Agreed. We'll produce a compatibility & regression matrix showing delta on your prompt set, and recommend fallback policies — e.g., automatic routing to older pinned model if divergence exceeds X.

[06:35] Elena Martinez: One more risk: some internal tooling hardcodes token limits; a migration will require our infra team to update ingestion. We need a migration playbook.
[06:43] Jordan Reyes: We'll draft a migration playbook with steps: pin, canary, shadow, eval, rollback, finalize. We'll highlight changes like tokenization differences and best practice patches.

[07:00] Priya Kapoor: Technical deep dive suggestion — run a bench with 100 concurrent summarization calls (4k tokens) on a dedicated pool with KV caching enabled to measure p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-call. I can run that if you provide a test endpoint and sample payloads.
[07:18] Tom Bradley: We can stand up a test VPC peer and provide sample payloads.
[07:22] Priya Kapoor: Great. Also: small note about transcriptions — sometimes the auto transcript shows V-P-C etc, sorry for the noise.

[30:10] (long section omitted in auto transcript)

[30:30] Jordan Reyes: Ok wrapping up — quick recap of agreed items. Jordan to send pricing and SOC2 pack. Priya to run the 4k token bench and the 2-week quantization eval. Liam to share the usage trend sheet and annotate cost spikes. Tom to provide infra diagrams and VPC details. We will plan a follow-up SE deep dive the week of Dec 27th.

[31:05] Sophie Lane: Sounds good, thank you.
[31:08] Elena Martinez: Appreciate the action items, we want to ensure the deprecation does not break user flows.
[31:13] Marcus Park: We'll also schedule procurement review after we get the committed pricing.

[31:25] Jordan Reyes: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
